partner_result_applied.equation_used: For T=aX^2+2bXY+affine with independent cap-one X,Y and b!=0, ||p_T||_p <= p|b|^(-1+1/p), in particular L3 and L2 bounds.

new_result.name: QFORM-EXTERNAL-COUPLING-NULL-PIVOT-C0-v1
new_result.scope: Distinct original coordinates X,Y,Z,U with A_XY=b!=0, A_YY=0, A_XZ=A_YZ=0, A_ZZ=gamma arbitrary, A_ZU=c!=0; every other coefficient arbitrary.
new_result.conclusion: p_Q belongs to C_0(R) and ||p_Q||_infinity <=3|b|^(-2/3)Psi(gamma,c), where Psi=2|gamma|^(-1/3) for |gamma|>=8|c| and Psi=(3/2)|c|^(-1/3)-|gamma|^(2/3)/(8|c|) otherwise. At gamma=0, ||p_Q||_infinity <=pq|b|^(-1+1/p)|c|^(-1/p), hence <=4/sqrt(|bc|) at p=2.
new_result.mechanism: Condition on all coordinates except X,Y,Z. The hyperbolic pair gives an Lp density; the Z receiver gives an Lq density either from its quadratic coefficient or from the random affine slope cU+d. Average the reciprocal affine slope using the cap-one fractional bathtub inequality. Continuity follows from Lp*Lq subset C0 and dominated conditional averaging.

unresolved_implication: The bare three-large-eigenvalue hypothesis has not been shown to force this original-coordinate hyperbolic-pair/external-coupling pattern with uniformly nondegenerate b,c, nor a grouped-coordinate analogue.
next_step: Apply the external-coupling rescue inside a current low-cross-rank or near-null structural survivor; otherwise derive a grouped-bank version in which a random affine receiver slope has an integrable reciprocal fractional moment before any fiber supremum.
